correctness.rationale: For coefficients c_k=n^{-1}1_{k<n}, g_k=p(1−p)^k, contraction triangle inequality gives an ℓ1 bound. The same unilateral shift S on ℓ∞ with sign-vector f(k)=sgn(c_k−g_k) attains equality for all n and p, so F_n(p)=2[(1−p)^n+Σ_{k<n}(g_k−1/n)_+]. For p=λ/n compact-uniform Riemann sums yield Φ(λ)=2e^(−λ) at λ≤1 and Φ=2[1−(1+log λ)/λ+e^(−λ)] at λ>1. Its derivative has a unique zero log λ=λ²e^(−λ), λ*=1.6946009205; initial interval [0,n/√(np)] mass testing rules out minimizing p with np→∞ and the geometric tail rules out np→0. Thus every minimizer np→λ*, minimum→κ≈.5646229252. Independent scipy bounded one-dimensional minima n=50,200,1000 tend to this root and limit; exact verifier script inspected. This is a universal operator-norm statement, not an individual T ergodic convergence claim.
